shared.validation_domain_needs_dot: Must contain at least one dot

traffic_engine.page_description: One DPI engine, two modes. Bypass carrier video throttling, or make HTTPS traffic look like a whitelisted service. Only one mode runs at a time.
traffic_engine.toast_video_enabled: Video Optimizer is now protecting video
traffic_engine.error_load_failed: The modem did not answer. Check the connection and try again.
traffic_engine.onboarding_description: One install unlocks both Video Optimizer and Masquerade.
traffic_engine.advanced_dialog_desc: Both modes share this engine, so removing it turns off Video Optimizer and Masquerade until you reinstall it.
traffic_engine.advanced_toast_error: Failed to remove the engine binary
traffic_engine.video_tagline: Counters carrier throttling of video so it buffers less.
traffic_engine.masquerade_tagline: Disguises HTTPS under one whitelisted domain so the carrier can't single it out to throttle.
traffic_engine.bypass_helper_external: Set elsewhere to TTL {{ttl}} / HL {{hl}} (TTL page or a SIM profile). Manage it there.
traffic_engine.kernel_module_hint: Install the kmod-nft-queue package on the modem, then reload this page.
traffic_engine.error_load_title: Could not read the Traffic Engine
traffic_engine.kernel_banner_desc: This firmware lacks the packet-queue support the engine needs, so neither mode can be turned on.
traffic_engine.bypass_hint: Carriers spot tethered devices by the hop count their packets arrive with. Pinning every packet to 64 makes devices behind the modem look like the modem itself.
traffic_engine.package_desc: The packet engine both modes share, and what it needs from the firmware.
traffic_engine.engine_desc: Pick a mode and watch the packets the engine handles.
traffic_engine.pkg_status_busy: Turn the engine off before removing it.
traffic_engine.pkg_status_idle: You can reinstall it from this page.
traffic_engine.mode_reason_kernel: This firmware lacks packet queue support, so no mode can run.
traffic_engine.strip_aria_video_one: The start of the handshake goes out as {{count}} one-byte piece, so the carrier never reads the hostname whole.
traffic_engine.strip_aria_video_other: The start of the handshake goes out as {{count}} one-byte pieces, so the carrier never reads the hostname whole.
traffic_engine.strip_aria_masquerade: Two decoy handshakes naming {{domain}} go out before the real one, so the carrier reads the disguise.
traffic_engine.hosts_empty_desc: Add a video CDN domain above, or restore the defaults.
traffic_engine.foot_switch_to_apply: Takes effect when you switch the engine to {{mode}}.
traffic_engine.foot_on_enable: Takes effect when you turn on {{mode}}.
traffic_engine.apply_blocked_other: {{mode}} is running. Switch modes to apply this.
traffic_engine.check_injection_confirmed_one: Fake SNI injection confirmed ({{count}} packet processed)
traffic_engine.check_injection_confirmed_other: Fake SNI injection confirmed ({{count}} packets processed)
traffic_engine.hosts_desc: The video CDN domains Video Optimizer works on.
traffic_engine.video_how: Carrier DPI reads the hostname in each handshake to spot video. Video Optimizer sends the start of the handshake in one-byte pieces, so the hostname never arrives whole and the video is not flagged.
traffic_engine.check_blocked: Turn on {{mode}} to run this check.
traffic_engine.masquerade_how: Before each real handshake, Masquerade sends two decoys naming the disguise domain. The carrier reads the decoy and treats the connection as that service.
traffic_engine.chart_aria_idle: No packets handled in the last 60 seconds
traffic_engine.chart_empty: Turn on a mode to see packets
traffic_engine.toast_install_error: Could not install the Traffic Engine
traffic_engine.chart_aria: Packets handled per second over the last 60 seconds, peaking at {{max}}

page.title: Ethernet Status
page.description: Monitor the ethernet link, limit its speed and set the LAN gateway.

strip.label: Ethernet port
strip.unavailable_body: Retrying every 10 seconds. Nothing has been changed.
strip.absent_body: This device has no ethernet port, so there is nothing to report or configure.

link.label: Link state
link.caption_up: Cable connected to the host port
link.caption_down: No cable detected on the host port

settings.title: Ethernet Port
settings.description: Set the port's link speed and how the modem powers its ethernet controller.
settings.consequence: Applying drops the link for a few seconds while the port renegotiates. You are on that link.
settings.consequence_applying: The link is down while the port renegotiates. This page confirms the new speed itself.
settings.consequence_unresponsive: The modem stopped answering, so this control is held until the next successful read.
settings.consequence_unread: The modem hasn't answered yet, so there is nothing to change until the first read lands.
settings.consequence_absent: There is no ethernet port to configure on this device.
settings.toast_confirm_error: Couldn't confirm the new speed. Check the link.
settings.aspm_hint: Active State Power Management (ASPM) lets the PCIe link to the ethernet controller doze between packets. Performance keeps it awake.
settings.aspm_consequence: Power saving modes can cause dropouts and added latency on the ethernet port. Applying does not drop the link.

lan_config.card_description: Set the router's LAN IP address (the gateway your devices use) and the size of the local network.
lan_config.help_gateway: The router's own address on the LAN. Devices use it as their default gateway.
lan_config.help_subnet: Choose the size of the LAN network as a CIDR prefix.
lan_config.confirm_body: The LAN will switch to {{address}} (netmask {{netmask}}). This rebinds the network and your current connection will drop.
lan_config.confirm_reconnect: After applying, the network rebinds and your connection drops briefly. A router or device using DHCP will reconnect automatically within a few seconds; one with a static IP must be moved to the new subnet manually. You'll then browse to the new address to continue.
lan_config.applied_body: The device is moving to {{address}}. Your connection will drop for about {{seconds}} seconds — reconnect your LAN or Ethernet cable, then open the new address:
lan_config.applied_body_auto: The device is moving to {{address}}. A router set to DHCP should reconnect on its own within about {{seconds}} seconds and pick up the new gateway. If it doesn't, reconnect your cable, then open the new address:
lan_config.reconnecting_auto_note: This page will open the new address automatically.
lan_config.error_invalid_ipaddr: Enter a valid unicast IPv4 address (e.g. 192.168.1.1).
lan_config.error_invalid_host_in_subnet: This is the network or broadcast address for the chosen subnet. Pick a usable host address.
lan_config.error_invalid_prefix: Choose a subnet prefix between /16 and /30.

errors.parse_failed: Failed to read the save response

dns.page_description: Override carrier-assigned DNS servers with your preferred resolvers for all devices on the local network.
dns.error_at_least_one: Enter at least one DNS server address
dns.toast_error_apply: Could not apply the DNS settings
dns.error_load_desc: The modem did not answer. Check the connection and try again.

errors.apply_failed: Could not apply the DNS settings

resolver.title: Resolver
resolver.description: Which DNS servers the devices on your network are given.

ipv4.title: IPv4 Servers
ipv4.description: Up to three, tried in order.

ipv6.title: IPv6 Servers
ipv6.description: Up to two, for devices that use IPv6.

mode.label: Custom DNS
mode.consequence_on: Devices on your network use the servers below.
mode.consequence_off: Devices use the servers your carrier assigns.

provider.label: Provider
provider.consequence: Fills both server lists. Editing an address makes it Custom.

ttl_mtu.page_description: Rewrite the hop count and packet size the modem puts on the cellular interface.

strip.label: In force now
strip.unavailable_body: The modem didn't answer. Nothing on it has been changed.
strip.idle_body: The modem is using the carrier's TTL and MTU exactly as negotiated. Turn one on below to change that.

banner.title: TTL and hop limit come from the {{profile}} profile
banner.body: Activating that profile writes both values, so this card is held to stop the two writers fighting. Change them in the profile, or activate a profile that leaves TTL unset.

ttl.title: TTL & Hop Limit
ttl.description: Applied to outbound packets on the cellular interface.

mtu.title: Maximum Transmission Unit
mtu.description: The largest packet the cellular interface will send without fragmenting.

shared.consequence_off: Turn the rewrite on to set a value.
shared.consequence_unread: The modem hasn't answered, so there is nothing to change yet.

rewrite.label: Rewrite the hop count
rewrite.consequence: Off means the modem forwards whatever hop count the client sent. Some carriers count hops to detect tethering.

ttl_value.label: TTL value
ttl_value.consequence: {{min}}–{{max}}. A device one hop behind the modem usually wants 64.

hl_value.label: Hop limit value
hl_value.consequence: The IPv6 equivalent. Set both unless you know the client is single-stack.

mtu_toggle.label: Override the MTU
mtu_toggle.consequence: Off restores the carrier-negotiated value on the cellular interface.

mtu_value.label: MTU value
mtu_value.consequence: {{min}}–{{max}}. Below roughly 1400 can break path-MTU discovery on sites that drop ICMP.
mtu_value.consequence_off: Turn the override on to set a value.

errors.value_range: TTL and hop limit must each be between {{min}} and {{max}}.
errors.no_value: Enter a TTL or a hop limit before applying.

ttl_mtu.toast_ttl_cleared: The modem is back on the carrier's own hop count.
ttl_mtu.toast_ttl_error: Couldn't apply the TTL and hop limit.
ttl_mtu.toast_mtu_cleared: MTU is back to the carrier-negotiated value.

page.title: IP Passthrough & USB
page.description: Hand the modem's public IP straight to one connected device instead of routing for the whole LAN.

blurb.eth: Set to hand the WAN IP to the Ethernet device
blurb.usb: Set to hand the WAN IP to the USB device

card.description: Applying writes every setting and reboots the modem.
card.network_description: Applied together with Passthrough, in one reboot.

mode.label: Mode
mode.description: Route the whole LAN, or pass the public IP to one device.

target.label: Target device
target.description: The device that receives the public IP.

nat.label: NAT
nat.description: With NAT suits almost every setup.

usb.label: USB connection
usb.description: The protocol used when the modem connects over USB.

dns.label: DNS proxy
dns.description: On, the modem answers DHCP DNS for the target device.

mode_note.rest: Ethernet or USB hands the WAN IP to one device, and the modem stops answering at its LAN gateway. Keep Tailscale or another way in.
mode_note.to_passthrough: Applying reboots the modem and this tab loses it. Afterwards the LAN gateway stops answering, so keep Tailscale or another way in.

dialog.title: Apply and reboot now?
dialog.body: The settings are written and the modem reboots immediately. This page hands off to the reboot countdown and signs you out.
dialog.body_gateway: Once passthrough is active the modem stops answering at its LAN gateway address. Make sure you have Tailscale, the passthrough device itself, or a serial console to get back in.
dialog.body_persist: The setting persists across further reboots.

ippt.toast_apply_error: Couldn't apply the IP Passthrough settings

errors.read_body: Nothing has been changed. Try again, or check that the modem is answering.
errors.card_unread: The modem hasn't answered yet, so there is nothing to change until the first read lands.
errors.mac_invalid: Enter a full MAC address, six pairs of hex digits.

device.label: Target device from connected list
device.empty: No connected devices found. Connect the device to the modem, then rescan.

locked_by_verizon.title: IP Passthrough is managed by your Verizon profile
locked_by_verizon.body: Active profile: "{{name}}". To change these settings, deactivate the profile from Custom Profiles.
locked_by_verizon.blocked: Your Verizon profile manages IP Passthrough.

masquerade.page_description: Make all HTTPS traffic appear as a whitelisted service to carrier DPI
masquerade.card_description: Make HTTPS traffic appear as a whitelisted service to carrier DPI.
masquerade.helper_domain: The domain that appears in the fake TLS handshake sent to the carrier.
masquerade.help_domain: Carriers read the SNI — the server name sent unencrypted in every TLS handshake — to decide what to throttle. Masquerade rewrites it to this domain so your traffic looks like that service.
masquerade.aria_domain_info: More information about the masquerade domain
masquerade.test_hint: A pass means your HTTPS handshakes are carrying the spoofed name, so the carrier sees this domain instead of the real one.
masquerade.aria_test_hint: What a passing injection test means
masquerade.test_description: Confirm fake SNI packets are being injected into HTTPS traffic

video_optimizer.page_description: Bypass carrier video throttling using DPI evasion on targeted video CDN hostnames
video_optimizer.card_description: Bypass carrier video throttling on cellular connections using DPI evasion.
video_optimizer.help_desync_repeats: Number of times the DPI-evading packet is sent for each matched flow. Higher values improve reliability when packets are lost or reordered, but increase CPU use and upstream bandwidth. Default 1 works for most users.
video_optimizer.helper_desync_repeats: Higher values resist stricter DPI but add a little overhead. 1 suits most networks.
video_optimizer.verify_hint: A pass means the engine is intercepting traffic to your hostlisted domains and applying DPI evasion.
video_optimizer.verify_description: Confirm DPI evasion is intercepting traffic for hostlisted domains
video_optimizer.hostlist_card_description: The video CDN domains Video Optimizer works on.
video_optimizer.toast_import_no_new: No new domains to import — all already in list
video_optimizer.dialog_restore_desc: This will replace the current list with the factory default CDN hostnames. Any custom domains you added will be removed.
